what: *** THE ERRAND IS ANSWERED: SHE IS IN THE PADRON, AT ANOTHER ADDRESS ***
the source: Montevideo, padron of 1850 (libro 264) - index ark 1:1:XMKF-FR3W, image ark 3:1:3QS7-89ZP-B99S-Z, plate read at apid TH-1961-36718-27970-97
result: *** LEONARDA LERENA, 11, BLANCA, ORIENTAL - AT CASA 229 OF CALLE SARANDI ***
what was already known: An errand was raised two hours earlier asking where she was, because she is absent from her parents' house in the same padron and this archive had used that absence to date the census.
what the plate says: *** She was never missing from the census - only from her parents' house. *** Born 20 February 1837, she is thirteen in 1850 and entered as *** eleven ***, which is ordinary. *** And the house number is a trap: *** her parents are at a casa 229 on another street entirely, and this is *** Sarandi 229 ***. *** TWO DIFFERENT HOUSES, BOTH NUMBERED 229, IN ONE PADRON *** - so 'household 229' has never been an identifier, and a file in this archive is named after it.

what: *** AND FOUR MORE PEOPLE CARRY THE SURNAME IN THAT HOUSE ***
the source: the same page, read line by line
result: *** ESTANISLADA, 20 | SINFORIANO, 19 | MANUELA, 60 | ROSA, 46 - every one entered as D.o, ditto, for LERENA ***
what was already known: This archive has documented five people held in slavery by this family, among them *** Barbara ***, named on an 1846 act as 'esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena', whose son was baptised with no surname of his own.
what the plate says: *** THE COLUMNS SAY WHAT THE NAMES DO NOT. *** Leonarda is *** blanca, oriental. *** Estanislada is *** morena ***; Sinforiano the same; *** MANUELA, sixty years old, is entered with patria AFRICA and estado casada ***; Rosa, forty-six, oriental, casada. *** Four adults of colour bearing the holder's surname, one of them African-born, living at an address where the only white person entered is an eleven-year-old girl. *** Slavery was abolished in Uruguay in 1842, so in 1850 they are legally free and still in the house, still under the name. *** That is the same pattern as Barbara's act, eight years later and four people wider. ***

the source: the limits of a census line
result: *** THE CENSUS DOES NOT SAY THEY WERE ENSLAVED, AND THIS FILE DOES NOT EITHER ***
what was already known: The padron has no column for condition; it has colour, patria and estado, and it is the combination that speaks.
what the plate says: *** What is established: four adults recorded with the Lerena surname by ditto, three of them morena and one born in Africa, at Sarandi 229 in 1850. *** What is inferred and *** FILED AS INFERENCE ***: that the surname reached them the way Barbara's reached her son. *** What would settle it: the parish registers for these four names at the Cordon or the Catedral, where a baptism or a burial would say 'liberta' or 'esclava de' outright *** - and the Cordon burial registers of 1839-1852 are already in this archive's hands, unread. *** They are entered as people in their own right, because no role is furniture. ***

what: *** THE HOLDER FORMULA, SWEPT ACROSS EVERY LERENA THIS ARCHIVE CAN NAME ***
the source: full text, the phrase 'esclava/esclavo/liberta de [holder]' run against each holder in turn, 12 October 2026
result: *** TWO POSITIVES, AND BOTH ARE HOUSEHOLDS THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HOLDS ***
what was already known: The four adults at Sarandi 229 carry the surname with no act to say how it reached them. The parish formula is the thing that would say it.
what the plate says: *** WORKS: 'esclava de Don Sancho Lerena' returns the Montevideo Catedral baptism of 1811-1813 *** - the act of 26 September 1812 for Maria Mercedes, daughter of Juana. *** WORKS: 'esclava de Don Alejandro Lerena' returns the San Jose de Mayo baptism AND burial of April 1846 *** - Barbara and her son Carmelo Anselmo. *** NOTHING: *** 'esclava de Don Pedro Antonio Lerena', 'esclava de Pedro Lerena', 'esclava de Luis Lerena', 'esclavo de Don Sancho Lerena', 'liberta de Don Pedro Lerena'. *** Two controls passing in the same form and session, so the nulls are real ones. ***

what: *** AND THE ABBREVIATION IS THE WHOLE OF IT ***
the source: the same phrase, written three ways
result: *** 'esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena' = NOTHING. 'esclava de Don Alejandro Lerena' = the two acts. 'esclava de Alejandro Lerena' = the two acts. ***
what was already known: The act itself, read at the transcript, says *** 'esclava de Don Alejandro Lerena' ***.
what the plate says: *** So the search tolerates a MISSING word and chokes on an ABBREVIATED one. *** D.n matches nothing; Don matches; dropping the honorific entirely matches. *** That is a narrow, exact rule and this archive's sources are full of D.n, D.a, S.n and V.a *** - every one of which will produce a confident empty page. Recorded in data/false-zeros.tsv.

what: *** WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE FOUR AT SARANDI 229 ***
the source: the sweep, read for what it does not find
result: *** NO ACT IN THE SEARCHABLE CORPUS NAMES A LERENA AS THEIR HOLDER ***
what was already known: Estanislada, Sinforiano, Manuela and Rosa carry the surname by ditto in the padron of 1850, and the census has no column for condition.
what the plate says: *** Three readings survive and the sweep does not choose between them. *** (1) Their acts use other wording - 'parda libre', 'morena libre', or a forename with no holder at all, which is how *** Barbara appears on the BURIAL *** even though the baptism names her holder. (2) They were held by someone else and took the name another way. (3) Their acts are not transcribed. *** What is now excluded is only the narrow thing: that a surviving, transcribed parish act says 'esclava de' and then names a Lerena this archive can name. *** The errand to read the Cordon burials 1839-1852 by eye stands, and is now the only route left.
